scope: Post-result descriptive audit of completed conditional and monitoring experiments; no new attacks, threshold selection, source promotion or raw-event re-evaluation
inputs: Only completed result metadata and the two hash-checked scene_metrics.jsonl.gz files. Verify code locks, source completion flags, shared baseline identities, all paired scene names and counters. Do not open native CAN files, event ledgers or reserved payloads.
outcomes: For each unchanged case and all/before/during/after/unavailable phase, recompute original gates per scene and count both_pass,candidate_only,comparator_only,both_fail. Every paired scene remains in the denominator; zero-request phases are failures and separately counted. Report candidate-minus-comparator percentage-point difference over all matched scenes.
statistics: Descriptive paired discordance counts only. Scenes may share drives, vehicles and recording dependencies. No independence assumption, p-values, confidence intervals, statistical significance or population generalization is claimed. Do not reconstruct pooled P95 by averaging scene P95s.
calibration: Retain every supplied model. Count valid, short, zero-sd and positive subnormal-sd models; report min/median/max positive sd. Subnormal means below Python binary64 minimum normal value and is a diagnostic, never a new variance floor. Preserve all numerical_failure request counts.
verification: Independent gate recalculation, paired-outcome Counter reduction and calibration summary from the saved per-scene evidence. Source hash checks and count validation are metadata checks, not a new reconstruction of underlying raw speed/attack events.
remaining_gaps: native reproduction of recent complete AV security methods with compatible inputs
real independently calibrated protected source and rollback-resistant evidence
